newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower on fund selling. Investment funds, holding sizeable long positions built up during the recent rally, were rolling forward some of their nearby holdings. Another factor for the decline was a more optimistic picture for the Brazilian 1997/98 crop. March lost $45 to close at $1,495 per tonne, while May gave up $49 to close at $1,510 per tonne.

In New York arabica futures raced higher, retracing early session losses and bouncing back from Tuesday's sharp decline, boosted by a late fund-led rally. Thursday is first notice day and the open interest remains quite large with certified coffee stocks at minimal levels.

Traders said there is talk of demand for deliveries of as much as 4,000 lots, which would not be able to be satisfied and this could lead the shorts having to scramble to cover positions and force the market higher still. March added 7.20 cents/lb to close at 175.30 cents/lb, while May closed 9.05 cents/lb higher at 166.30 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 1.05 to 7.80 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - Brazil faces a serious deficit in coffee supplies, according to the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Producers (Abecafe) which released its first estimate for the 1997/98 (May/April) crop year. Abecafe secretary general Jose Sette said that based on the Associations' production estimate of 23.2 million 60-kg bags Brazil will have a deficit of 4 million bags.

The 1997/98 figure compares to 1996/97 production of 27.5 million bags. Jose Braz Matielo, coordinator for Procafe, an arm of Brazil's Minsitry of Agriculture, recently said that Brazil's 1997/98 coffee harvest can be estimated at between 17 and 21 million bags. However, Abecafe said that the low estimates have very little credibility, adding that the figure of 23.2 million bags can be regarded as conservative.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 1.851 million bags of coffee in November 1996, down from the 2.192 million bags exported in October but significantly up on the 986,100 bags shipped in November 1995. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (April/May) up to 11.089 million bags, 7.8 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995/96.

Total exports in crop year 1995/96 dropped to 13.7 million bags from 15.9 million bags the previous year. Main countries of destination for green coffee in April/November 1996 were Germany (1.112 vs 0.629 million bags), the United States (1.649 vs 1.548 million bags) and Japan (845,700 vs 678,900 bags).

Main destinations for solubles were Germany (88,100 vs 101,200 bags), Russia (548,400 vs 787,400 bags), the Ukraine (174,100 vs 6,500 bags), the United States (358,900 vs 251,800 bags) and Japan (161,700 vs 152,400 bags).

UGANDA - According to the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) coffee exports in January 1997 totalled 551,668 60-kg bags valued at $38.56 million, versus 514,394 bags worth $35.85 million in December. This brought total exports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 1.843 million bags valued at $133.8 million against 1.348 million bags valued at $138.2 million in the same period last season.

The UCDA attributed the rise in volume to the high level of closing stocks at the end of 1995/96 and a heavy harvest in central and easter regions. Average export prices reflected the international market, rising to mid-January levels of $1.32 from $1.21 in December 1996.

FINLAND - Finland imported 947,100 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 47 per cent more than was imported the same period the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 44 per cent to 758,500 bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Costa Rica (107,900 vs 95,700 bags), Guatemala (141,000 vs 80,600 bags), Brazil (146,100 vs 106,000 bags) and Colombia (213,400 vs 166,000 bags). The country exported 130,800 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 69 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply to 96,800 bags from 217,500 bags in 1994.
